title: Black Pepper Tofu
description: Crispy-coated tofu tossed in a buttery, aggressively peppery sauce with caramelized shallots and chiles. The amount of black pepper here is not a typo — it's what makes the dish.

ingredients.name: sweet soy sauce (kecap manis)
ingredients.notes: or 2 tbsp soy sauce + 1 tbsp brown sugar

steps.text: Cut each tofu block into 1-inch cubes and pat thoroughly dry with paper towels — every bit of moisture you remove is more crispiness you gain. Toss cubes gently with cornstarch until evenly coated, shaking off excess.

Heat vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet or wok over high heat until shimmering. Add tofu in a single layer (work in batches if needed) and cook undisturbed until golden and crisp on the bottom, 3 to 4 minutes. Flip and crisp the other side, about 3 more minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium and add butter to the same pan. Once melted and foaming, add shallots and cook, stirring often, until softened and beginning to caramelize at the edges, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add garlic and chiles and cook for 1 minute. Stir in sweet soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, and black pepper. Let the sauce bubble and thicken for 30 seconds.
Return tofu to the pan along with scallions. Toss gently to coat everything in the sauce, cooking for another minute until heated through. Serve immediately over steamed rice.

inspirations.author: Yotam Ottolenghi
inspirations.note: Based on Ottolenghi's iconic black pepper tofu from Plenty, widely adapted by NYT and food blogs
